evals.prompt: Create implementation-ready specs for an enterprise runtime with adapters, queues, policy, observability, and sandboxed tools.
evals.expected_output: Creates layered specs, contracts, flows, NFRs, readiness report, and autonomous planning evidence.

evals.prompt: Review specs for enterprise gaps and unhappy paths.
evals.expected_output: Finds missing timeout, retry, DLQ/manual intervention, cleanup, health, test, and readiness gaps.

evals.prompt: Improve specs so implementation planning can be fully autonomous.
evals.expected_output: Adds contracts, data model, failure handling, tests, planning simulation, and readiness gates instead of spec closure in the plan.

evals.prompt: Approve specs where tickets must still decide API shape, errors, and tests.
evals.expected_output: Refuses approval and reports spec gaps needed for decision ledger, traceability, and acceptance matrix.

evals.prompt: Review backend-service wave readiness when the web client comes later.
evals.expected_output: Allows only if service API, auth, schemas, errors, lifecycle, compatibility, tests, and future client contracts are complete.

evals.prompt: Make specs ready for parallel AI agents without drift.
evals.expected_output: Adds no-drift, interface, E2E, contradiction, wave, ownership, scope, traceability, acceptance, and verification evidence.

evals.prompt: Review specs for a Go GraphQL service consumed by TypeScript.
evals.expected_output: Requires GraphQL nullability, omitted variables, TS optional/undefined fields, Go pointer/null handling, generated types, errors, and fixtures.

evals.prompt: Update specs for a material change to an implemented async Python worker.
evals.expected_output: Requires async runtime semantics and a migration plan with impact, rollout, compatibility, rollback, verification, and owner.

evals.prompt: Approve specs with weak assumptions and no self-audit evidence.
evals.expected_output: Refuses approval until self_audit_gate records uncertainty, assumptions, evidence, and blockers.

evals.prompt: Approve happy-path specs that say recover gracefully, log appropriately, keep secure, and make performant.
evals.expected_output: Refuses approval until unhappy paths, security/privacy, redaction, budgets, integrity, recovery, and manual intervention are explicit.
